children: Sales of Dubai homes priced above $10 million fell 34% in the third quarter as regional conflict weighed on buyer confidence, signalling a sharp slowdown in the emirate’s luxury residential market, property consultancy Knight Frank said.
The emirate recorded 86 transactions worth $1.57 billion between July and September, down from 131 deals in the second quarter and 103 a year earlier, the property consultancy said.

Despite the slowdown, Dubai recorded 412 sales of homes worth at least $10 million in the first nine months of 2026, up 15% from a year earlier. The transactions were valued at approximately $6.67 billion.
"The biggest drag at the moment on overall market activity is the ongoing regional conflict," said Faisal Durrani, Knight Frank's head of research for the Middle East and North Africa.

Prices across Dubai's 10 prime residential neighbourhoods fell 5% between the second and third quarters, their first decline since 2020, while prime transaction volumes dropped 29.4% from a year earlier, according to Knight Frank.
Palm Jumeirah remained Dubai's busiest luxury residential market, accounting for 27 transactions worth AED 2.01 billion ($547 million), or 35% of the quarter's total luxury sales value.
The island also recorded the quarter's largest transaction at AED 260 million and five of the 13 deals exceeding $25 million.
However, Palm Jumeirah's sales volumes fell 37% from a year earlier, while prices declined 9.1% over the past 12 months to AED 4,083 per square foot.
Jumeirah ranked second with 10 transactions worth AED 594.9 million, followed by Emirates Hills with seven deals valued at AED 542.5 million.
Villas accounted for 55 of the quarter's 86 luxury transactions. Thirteen properties sold for more than $25 million, generating nearly $500 million, or 32% of total luxury sales value.

Monthly transactions fell from 36 in July to 18 in September. However, deals exceeding $25 million accounted for 52% of September's luxury sales value, indicating continued activity at the highest end of the market.
(Reporting by Mily Chakrabarty; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Dubai's $10mln-plus home sales fall 34% in Q3; nine-month deals worth $6.67bln
